# Re-reading the Problem

"You need to **wait in line for 10 minutes** to make a call."

The **10-minute wait** is just context about how long you stand in line — it does **not** affect the call's cost (since you're not talking on the phone yet).

The cost depends only on the **36-minute call duration**:

## Recalculating

**First 16 minutes** at $0.25/min:
$$16 \times \$0.25 = \$4.00$$

**Remaining 20 minutes** at $0.20/min:
$$20 \times \$0.20 = \$4.00$$

## Final Answer

$$\$4.00 + \$4.00 = \boxed{\$8.00}$$

The 36-minute call costs **$8.00** (the 10-minute wait is not part of the billed call time).

content.text:
# Cost of a 36-Minute Payphone Call

## Setting Up the Problem

The call has **two pricing tiers**:
- **First 16 minutes:** $0.25 per minute
- **After 16 minutes:** $0.20 per minute

## Calculating Each Portion

**First 16 minutes:**
$$16 \text{ min} \times \$0.25/\text{min} = \$4.00$$

**Remaining time:** 36 − 16 = 20 minutes at the reduced rate
$$20 \text{ min} \times \$0.20/\text{min} = \$4.00$$

## Total Cost

$$\$4.00 + \$4.00 = \boxed{\$8.00}$$

A 36-minute call would cost **$8.00**.
